# Required status checks on `main`, as configured in branch protection.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#
# GitHub's branch protection stores required status checks as a list of literal
# CONTEXT NAMES. A matrix job's context name is derived from the job's `name:`
# template and its matrix values, so editing either one in `ci.yml` renames the
# contexts — and protection keeps requiring the OLD names. Those names can no
# longer be produced by any run, so every PR waits forever on a check that will
# never report. The result is a repository that cannot be merged into, caused by
# an edit that looked purely cosmetic and whose CI was fully green.
#
# This is not hypothetical here: it has already happened to this repo once, when
# the single `test` job became a three-way Node matrix.
#
# `test/required-status-checks.test.mjs` derives the context names that `ci.yml`
# ACTUALLY produces today and asserts they equal this list. So a matrix edit
# turns red in CI, in the same PR that made it, with a message naming the exact
# `gh api` call needed — instead of silently wedging `main` after the merge.
#
# HOW TO CHANGE THE MATRIX
#
# 1. Edit `ci.yml`. CI now fails, on purpose.
# 2. Update this file to the new names. CI goes green.
# 3. The PR is still unmergeable: protection requires the old names. Update it:
#
#      gh api repos/edgeorgie/agentlens/rulesets \
#        --jq '.[] | select(.target=="branch") | .id'
#      gh api -X PUT repos/edgeorgie/agentlens/rulesets/<id> --input <edited.json>
#
#    (`main` is protected by a RULESET, not classic branch protection. See
#    `scripts/check-live-protection.mjs` for why it was migrated.)
# 4. Re-run the PR's checks. The new contexts report and the PR merges.
#
# Step 3 needs admin on the repo, so it cannot be done from inside a workflow
# run. That is why this mirror exists at all: the test cannot fix the drift, but
# it can refuse to let it land unnoticed.
#
# WHAT THIS FILE DOES NOT PROVE
#
# This mirror plus its test prove `mirror == workflow`. They cannot prove
# `mirror == live protection`, and live protection is what actually wedges
# `main`. That second half is now checked directly by the `protection-drift` job
# in ci.yml, which reads the live ruleset from the REST API on every `main` push
# and on a daily schedule — possible because rulesets are readable with
# `metadata: read`, where classic protection needed `administration` and so was
# invisible to `GITHUB_TOKEN`. So: this file catches a drifting PR at review
# time, and that job catches a drifting repository SETTING, which no PR-time
# check can observe.
#
# Blank lines and `#` comments are ignored. One context name per line.
